dispositions.title: Decorator provenance with class-level BFF exports
dispositions.intentional_contract: A Pytincture backend_for_frontend class decorator exports its public methods and public read-only attributes. Method-level export declarations are not required.
dispositions.security_boundary: Static discovery accepts security decorators only when their exact binding is proven to come directly from pytincture or pytincture.dataclass at that point in source order.

dispositions.title: Same-origin browser trust with application-owned assets
dispositions.intentional_contract: Application-selected browser Python and manifest-approved widget JavaScript execute as trusted same-origin application code. That same-origin execution model is intentional and is not a sandbox boundary.
dispositions.security_boundary: Direct assets are deliberately unauthenticated, but must belong to a real application and an explicit application browser/public/favicon/widget declaration. Python is never public, and SVG responses cannot create a same-origin script context.
regression_tests: pytincture/frontend/e2e-tests/pytincture.spec.mjs::direct SVG navigation cannot execute application-origin script

dispositions.title: Stateless SAML browser binding and duplicate-delivery boundary
dispositions.intentional_contract: SAML browser transactions use signed HttpOnly cookies and remain portable across workers without Redis, process memory, or sticky routing.
dispositions.security_boundary: Pytincture rejects cross-browser login CSRF and normal sequential replay. Without shared mutable state, exactly one of two simultaneous raw requests carrying the same valid pre-response cookie and assertion cannot be guaranteed to win.
dispositions.optional_control: A deployment that requires strict simultaneous single-consumption must add a shared atomic transaction-consumption control. That policy does not make Redis a Pytincture requirement.
